function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single person—rather, it was gradually understood over centuries through the work of many scientists and thinkers.

| Era | Key Figures | Contributions |
|-----|-------------|---------------|
| **Ancient Greece** | Thales of Miletus (600 BCE) | Noted static electricity from rubbing amber. |
| **17th–18th Century** | William Gilbert (1544‑1603) | Published *De Magnete* (1600), distinguishing magnetism from static electricity and coined the term “electricity.” |
| **18th Century** | Benjamin Franklin (1706‑1790) | Conducted kite experiments, proposed the concept of positive/negative charge, and introduced the idea of electrical charge conservation. |
| **Late 18th Century** | Alessandro Volta (1745‑1827) | Invented the voltaic pile (the first battery) in 1800, providing a steady source of electric current. |
| **19th Century** | Michael Faraday (1791‑1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction (1831), laying groundwork for electric generators and motors. |
| **19th Century** | James Clerk Maxwell (1831‑1879) | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations, predicting electromagnetic waves. |

So while ancient Greeks observed static electricity, the systematic scientific understanding—and practical harnessing—of electricity emerged through the cumulative work of these and many other researchers.
